title: klax audit event v1
description: A synchronous event in the klax audit protocol. turn.start is an execution gate; turn.finish reports a completed turn. Stream consumers ignore unknown properties and unknown v1 event names; a command bound to one exact event may reject a different event.

event.description: Namespaced event type. Known v1 values are turn.start and turn.finish. Stream consumers ignore unknown values; a command bound to one exact event may reject a different event.

turn.description: Self-contained snapshot of the turn. turn.finish repeats the turn.start fields so it can be processed independently.

turn_id.description: Lowercase hex of the first 20 bytes of SHA-256 over the exact compact Go encoding/json byte sequence ["klax.turn/v1", session_key, session_created, turn_seq]. Go's default HTML escaping applies. Unique within one uninterrupted klax state store; independent stores can produce the same value and aggregators key by their own (installation_id, turn_id).

turn_seq.description: Durable monotonically increasing turn sequence within this session incarnation's queue.

accepted_at.description: UTC time when klax durably accepted the inbound request.

start_at.description: UTC time when the turn.start audit boundary was reached, before the start hook and backend.

finish_at.description: UTC time when klax formed the final turn result at the turn.finish boundary, before the finish hook and final delivery.

origin.description: Immutable transport coordinates of the accepted inbound request.

transport.description: Public audit transport name, currently tg, max, vk, ym, or ui. Internal routing prefixes such as mx can differ.

id.description: Transport-native chat identifier without the klax transport prefix.

thread_id.description: Transport-native topic or thread identifier, when available.

message.description: Transport-native message identity. For UI requests, id is the client nonce.

id.description: Message identifier or UI request nonce.

sender.description: Transport-native sender identity, as known at acceptance time.

routing.description: The durable klax session selected for this turn.

session_key.description: Canonical klax routing key. It can represent a transport chat or a cross-transport mapped user.

session_created.description: Opaque persisted store-wide session incarnation, not a timestamp. Together with session_key and turn_seq it forms turn_id.

session_name.description: User-visible session name at the turn.start boundary.

request.description: The received request and the exact prompt submitted to the backend.

original_text.description: Text as accepted from the transport, before group-trigger removal and prompt canonicalization.

effective_prompt.description: Exact prompt passed to the backend after trigger processing, canonicalization, and attachment path materialization.

attachments.description: Files materialized for this turn, in stable inbound attachment order (the NN component of the durable filename).

name.description: Run-view basename visible to the backend after collision disambiguation.

path.description: Absolute path to the durable session-store file. It was readable by klax at snapshot construction but consumers must handle concurrent removal.

sha256.description: Lowercase SHA-256 of the durable file bytes.

execution.description: Backend launch configuration fixed at the turn.start boundary.

backend_session_id.description: Backend session identifier. turn.finish can populate it when it became known during the run.

model_requested.description: Explicit per-session model override, when configured.

effort.description: Explicit reasoning or thinking override, when configured.

sandbox.description: Requested backend sandbox mode, when configured.

tty.description: Whether klax launched the backend through its TTY integration.

append_system_prompt.description: Additional system prompt supplied by the operator.

result.description: Terminal result, present only in turn.finish events.

output.description: Final answer prepared for delivery, when present. Partial output can accompany an error or aborted result.

error.description: Terminal error details for error or aborted results.

stage.description: Subsystem that produced the error. Known v1 values are klax and backend.

code.description: Stable machine-readable error classification. Known v1 values are aborted, run-start-failed, and backend-failed; consumers treat unknown future v1 values as generic errors.

model_used.description: Model reported by the completed backend run.

tokens.description: Token accounting reported for this backend turn.

context_after.description: Canonical session context snapshot after a successful turn.

used.description: Context tokens in use after the turn.

elapsed_ms.description: Non-negative phase durations in milliseconds. total is exactly queued + start_hook + backend + finalize, not an independently measured wall-clock span.

start_hook.description: Time spent in the synchronous turn.start hook.

finalize.description: Backend return to the turn.finish boundary, including klax persistence.

total.description: Exact sum of queued, start_hook, backend, and finalize.

trace.description: Optional turn.finish trace. blocks is the ordinary klax UI normalization of the exact raw range.

label.description: Unstable human-readable UI presentation; consumers must not parse it.

path.description: Absolute path to the backend JSONL transcript read by klax for this snapshot.

from_event.description: Zero-based physical event index of the backend user record durably bound to this klax turn.

to_event.description: Exclusive physical event index after the last complete record observed for the turn.

sha256.description: Lowercase SHA-256 of the exact contiguous physical JSONL bytes for [from_event,to_event), including original line terminators.
